requirement: Normalize FlaskBB self-registration identities consistently. Trim leading/trailing whitespace from username and email; preserve username display case, and lowercase email. Registration validators, failure hooks and stored users must see the same normalized identity. Do not mutate the caller's frozen UserRegistrationInfo. Preserve the existing object identity when no field needs normalization, because existing plugins rely on it. UsernameUniquenessValidator and EmailUniquenessValidator must also reject ASCII case variants and surrounding whitespace when invoked directly against existing users. Keep password, language and group unchanged. Preserve original public import paths, registration exceptions, plugins and unrelated forum functionality.

Continue the prior identity change. Self-registration must reject a requested primary group that does not exist (including None), or whose current database flags include admin, super_mod, mod, guest or banned. Reject via StopValidation containing a reason with attribute 'group'; invoke the normal registration failure hook once and do not persist a user or call post-processors. Accept any existing group with all five flags false, including newly created ordinary groups; do not hardcode allowed or forbidden IDs. This guard must apply even when no plugin validators are registered. Existing validation failures and all prior identity rules must remain correct. Preserve original public APIs and unrelated forum functionality.

Continue the prior identity and group changes. When registration validation fails, attempt the registration failure hook exactly once. If that hook raises an ordinary Exception, the caller must still receive the original StopValidation with its original reasons; when a validator raised a StopValidation instance directly, preserve that exact instance. Never persist a user or call post-processors on this failure path. Do not swallow BaseException subclasses such as KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit. Keep successful registration and post-processor exception behavior unchanged, and preserve all earlier requirements and original public APIs.
